analysis:
Market regime is a mild uptrend (SPY +0.4% vs SMA50, 20d slope +1.25%) — constructive but not euphoric. The portfolio is 62% deployed across 4 positions, all slightly underwater but none at thesis-break levels: AMP (-0.90%), BR (-2.54%), MCO (-1.96%) are minor losses well within their stop bands; NVDA (+1.15%) is the only current winner and the only candidate reappearing on the screen with exceptional fundamentals (105% rev growth, 66% op margin, PEG 0.45, +22.6% EPS revision). No existing position shows a thesis break — all four are quality businesses in an uptrend; recommend holding with current stops.

The historical performance demands humility: 10% win rate, 0.03 profit factor, Sortino -13.17. This is a clear signal to be very selective with new entries and to avoid forcing trades to manufacture activity. The bar for any new buy is genuine asymmetry: basing in lower 52w range, quality fundamentals, and a risk/reward above 2.5x.

Scanning the 30 candidates: most are extended (PSX at 100% of range +20.5% above SMA50, APA at 93%, COP at 86%, ZBRA at 81%). A handful have basing setups in the lower half of the range. TEL (TE Connectivity) stands out as the most disciplined entry: 24% of 52w range, only +0.3% above SMA50 (just emerging from base), forward P/E 16, PEG 0.87, ROE 23.3%, op margin 20.8%, solid FCF of $2.3B, and a modest +2.3% EPS revision. It is a Stage 1 to Stage 2 transition candidate — exactly what the strategy targets. Risk/reward is ~2.8x with proper stops. Earnings are 40 days out (Oct 28) which is a known catalyst risk; position sizing is reduced accordingly and an earnings-eve exit rule is included. No other candidate clears both the technical (basing, not extended) and fundamental bars simultaneously with sufficient asymmetry to justify a second new trade given available headroom of ~$31k and the imperative to preserve capital.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $206.00 or better on any intraday dip; if price gaps above $208 without a pullback, skip the trade and wait for a retest of the SMA50 (~$205). Do not chase.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: TE Connectivity is a high-quality industrial connector and sensor business with 23.3% ROE, 20.8% operating margin, $2.3B FCF, and accelerating revenue growth (+13.8%). Forward P/E of 16 with PEG 0.87 represents fair-to-cheap valuation for the quality level. EPS revisions are modestly positive (+2.3%). The business is a secular beneficiary of EV/electrification and industrial automation tailwinds. TECHNICAL: TEL is basing at just 24% of its 52-week range (well off the $246 high), trading only +0.3% above its SMA50 — the textbook Stage 1-to-2 transition the strategy targets. SMA50 slope is flat-to-slightly-positive (+0.1%), suggesting the base is stabilizing. ATR is 3.1% of price, giving clean stop placement at 1.75x ATR below entry (~5.3%) without being too wide or too tight. Risk/reward to prior high zone (~$238) is approximately 2.9:1.
trades.exit_plan: 1) Stop hit at $195.10 — exit immediately, no averaging down. 2) Earnings eve (Oct 27) — if position is profitable, consider trimming 50% before the Oct 28 report to avoid binary event risk; if at a loss approaching stop, exit fully before earnings. 3) Thesis break: if TEL drops back below its SMA200 on volume or EPS revisions turn negative, exit regardless of stop level. 4) Time stop: if no progress toward $215 within 8 weeks, reassess and consider closing to redeploy. 5) Target $238 — take partial profits (50%) and trail stop on remainder toward SMA50.
